title: Customer Churn Analysis Report
executive_summary: Analysis of 749 customers reveals an overall churn rate of 37.7%. Monthly-contract customers churn at more than double the rate of annual-contract customers. A high-risk segment of 100 customers with heavy support usage and low satisfaction churns at 71.0%. Premium-plan customers generate lifetime value nearly 4× that of Basic customers, underscoring the revenue impact of retaining higher-tier subscribers.

key_findings.statement: The dataset contains 749 customers with an overall churn rate of 37.7% and a mean monthly fee of $42.11.
Churn rates differ modestly across plans: Basic is highest at 38.9%, followed by Standard at 36.7%, and Premium at 36.6%. The spread between Basic and Premium is approximately 2.3 percentage points.

Churn by signup cohort shows the 2024 cohort is highest at 39.8%, followed by 2021 at 38.0%, 2023 at 37.1%, and 2022 at 36.7%. The 2024 cohort's elevated rate may reflect insufficient tenure to build loyalty.

Contract type is a strong churn driver. Monthly-contract customers churn at 48.3% versus 21.9% for annual-contract customers — monthly churn is 121.1% higher than annual, representing an increase in churn risk for month-to-month subscribers.

100 customers meet the at-risk criteria (≥5 support tickets and satisfaction score ≤2). This segment churns at 71.0%, nearly double the overall rate, making it the highest-priority intervention target.

Customer tenure averages 20.8 months (median 19.0, SD 13.2), indicating a wide spread in customer longevity. Mean satisfaction is 3.4 out of 5; 27 customers have a missing satisfaction score, limiting satisfaction-based analyses.

Mean lifetime value rises sharply by plan: Basic $463, Standard $869, Premium $1,817. Premium LTV is 292.0% higher than Basic, confirming that retaining Premium customers delivers outsized revenue value.

limitations: 27 customers have missing satisfaction scores, which may introduce bias into satisfaction-based segmentation and the at-risk filter.
The 2024 cohort has shorter observable tenure than earlier cohorts, so its elevated churn rate may partly reflect truncated observation windows rather than a genuine behavioural difference.
Lifetime value is computed as a mean per plan and does not account for discounts, promotions, or variable usage fees that could affect true revenue.
The at-risk segment definition (tickets ≥5 and satisfaction ≤2) is a heuristic threshold; alternative cut-offs could materially change segment size and churn rate.
The dataset is a single snapshot; longitudinal tracking would be needed to confirm causal relationships between contract type, satisfaction, and churn.
conclusion: Churn is elevated across all segments at ~37.7%, but contract type and support experience are the clearest differentiators. Converting monthly subscribers to annual contracts and proactively addressing the 100 at-risk customers (71.0% churn rate) represent the highest-impact near-term interventions. Given Premium customers' LTV of $1,817 — 292% above Basic — targeted retention investment for Premium subscribers is strongly justified.
